speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Radiculopathy (likely L5 or S1 nerve root compression due to acute disc herniation).

Given your age and the sudden onset of sharp pain radiating down your leg into your foot during exercise, this is highly suggestive of a herniated disc compressing a nerve root. The MRI results should confirm the location and severity of the disc protrusion, but based on your description of radiation to the foot and the mechanism of injury, lumbar radiculopathy is the primary diagnosis. I will wait for the MRI to rule out cauda equina syndrome, but please report immediately if you experience loss of bowel or bladder control.
